title: AA10: sender already constructed
summary: The EntryPoint rejected account creation because the sender smart account already has code deployed, but the UserOperation still included factory/initCode deployment data.
likelyCauses: The client is resubmitting a first-use UserOperation after the account was already deployed.
The account address was derived correctly, but stale factory or initCode data is still being attached.
The sender address belongs to an existing smart account on this network.
nextSteps: Check whether the sender address already has contract code on the target chain.
Remove initCode, or the v0.7/v0.8 factory and factoryData fields, when sending from an already deployed account.
If this was meant to deploy a new account, recompute the counterfactual sender and factory calldata.

title: AA13: initCode failed or OOG
summary: The account deployment path failed before the smart account was created: the factory/initCode reverted, ran out of gas, or could not complete account creation.
likelyCauses: The factory address or encoded factory call is wrong for this account type or chain.
The account does not have enough native token to pay for deployment when no paymaster is covering the operation.
verificationGasLimit is too low for the factory and account initialization code.
nextSteps: Decode the initCode or v0.7/v0.8 factory and factoryData fields and verify the factory address and calldata.
Simulate the factory call directly or with a trace tool to capture the inner revert.
Increase verificationGasLimit only if tracing shows the deployment path is running out of gas.

title: AA14: initCode must return sender
summary: The factory/initCode returned an account address that does not match the UserOperation sender address expected by the EntryPoint.
likelyCauses: The sender was computed from different factory calldata than the calldata submitted to the bundler.
The factory returns a deployed address that differs from the counterfactual sender.
The UserOperation was assembled for the wrong account factory, salt, owner, or chain.
nextSteps: Recompute the counterfactual sender from the exact factory address, salt, owner, and initialization calldata.
Verify that the factory returns the same address as the UserOperation sender.
Regenerate the UserOperation after fixing the factory calldata rather than only resubmitting it.

title: AA15: initCode must create sender
summary: The account creation path completed without leaving contract code at the sender address, so the EntryPoint still sees an undeployed account.
likelyCauses: The factory call returned without deploying the smart account.
The factory deployed a different address than the sender address in the UserOperation.
The factory implementation does not return or create the sender expected by this EntryPoint flow.
nextSteps: Check the sender address for code immediately after simulating the factory call.
Verify that the factory deploys the account at the exact sender address and returns it.
Fix the factoryData or initCode path before retrying the UserOperation.

title: AA20: account not deployed
summary: EntryPoint v0.6 could not validate the sender because the account is not deployed and the UserOperation did not include initCode to deploy it.
likelyCauses: The sender address is counterfactual, but the first UserOperation omitted initCode.
The UserOperation is being sent to the wrong network, where the account has not been deployed.
The client is using an incorrect sender address for the account owner or factory.
nextSteps: Check whether the sender has code on the chain where the bundler is simulating.
For a first transaction on EntryPoint v0.6, include valid initCode.
Confirm the chain, EntryPoint address, account factory, and sender address all belong to the same deployment.

title: AA22: expired or not due
summary: The account validation data says the UserOperation is outside its allowed validity window: either expired after validUntil or not yet usable before validAfter.
likelyCauses: A time-bounded signature or session key expired before bundler inclusion.
validAfter is set in the future, so the operation is not due yet.
The client populated validity timestamps when the account expected zero or a different window.
nextSteps: Compare validAfter and validUntil with the current block timestamp on the target chain.
Create a fresh signature or session authorization with a valid time window.
If the account does not use time windows, set the validity fields to the account's expected neutral values.

title: AA30: paymaster not deployed
summary: EntryPoint v0.6 found a paymaster address in paymasterAndData, but that paymaster contract is not deployed on the target chain.
likelyCauses: The first 20 bytes of paymasterAndData point to the wrong address.
The paymaster exists on a different chain or EntryPoint deployment.
The client attached stale sponsorship data from another environment.
nextSteps: Decode the first 20 bytes of paymasterAndData and verify that address has contract code.
Regenerate paymasterAndData for the same chain and EntryPoint version as the UserOperation.
If no paymaster should be used, remove paymasterAndData and ensure the sender can prefund gas.

title: AA32: paymaster expired or not due
summary: The paymaster validation data says the sponsorship is outside its allowed validity window: expired after validUntil or not yet usable before validAfter.
likelyCauses: The paymaster signature or sponsorship response expired before submission.
The sponsorship is not active yet according to the paymaster's validation data.
The client reused paymaster data from an old quote or a different policy window.
nextSteps: Request fresh paymaster data immediately before submitting the UserOperation.
Check the paymaster's validAfter and validUntil values against the target chain timestamp.
Confirm the Gas Manager or paymaster policy is active for this app, chain, and operation.

title: AA34: paymaster signature error
summary: The paymaster's authorization or signature validation failed, so the EntryPoint will not let that paymaster sponsor the UserOperation.
likelyCauses: The paymaster signature is malformed, expired, or signed for different UserOperation fields.
The client is using the wrong field layout for the EntryPoint version: paymasterAndData in v0.6 versus paymaster/paymasterData fields in v0.7/v0.8.
The paymaster policy rejected the operation even though a paymaster address was supplied.
nextSteps: Request fresh paymaster data from the sponsorship service for this exact UserOperation.
Verify the EntryPoint version and paymaster field layout used by the client.
Check the paymaster policy, chain allowlist, and signing key configuration before resubmitting.

title: AA26: over verificationGasLimit
summary: EntryPoint v0.7/v0.8 account or paymaster validation used more gas than the UserOperation's verificationGasLimit allowed.
likelyCauses: The smart account's validateUserOp path is more expensive than estimated.
Paymaster validation is included in the shared verification gas budget for this EntryPoint version.
Manual gas overrides capped verificationGasLimit below the simulated requirement.
nextSteps: Run eth_estimateUserOperationGas or your bundler's simulation endpoint again with the final UserOperation fields.
Raise verificationGasLimit only after checking that account validation logic is expected to cost that much.
Remove stale manual gas overrides that force verificationGasLimit below the current estimate.

title: AA36: over paymasterVerificationGasLimit
summary: EntryPoint v0.7/v0.8 paymaster validation exceeded the paymasterVerificationGasLimit assigned to the UserOperation.
likelyCauses: validatePaymasterUserOp needs more gas than the client or paymaster service supplied.
The paymaster policy path is unusually expensive for this operation, token, or account.
Manual gas overrides reduced paymasterVerificationGasLimit below the bundler estimate.
nextSteps: Request new paymaster data and gas estimates for the exact final UserOperation.
Increase paymasterVerificationGasLimit if the paymaster operator expects this validation cost.
Ask the paymaster operator to simplify or fix validation if the required gas looks abnormal.

title: AA40: over verificationGasLimit
summary: EntryPoint v0.6 account or paymaster verification used more gas than the UserOperation's verificationGasLimit allowed.
likelyCauses: The smart account or paymaster validation path is more expensive than estimated.
The client submitted stale gas estimates after changing calldata, signature, paymaster data, or account state.
Manual overrides capped verificationGasLimit below the gas consumed during validation.
nextSteps: Re-run UserOperation gas estimation after all signatures and paymaster fields are final.
Increase verificationGasLimit only if the validation path is expected to cost that much.
Trace validateUserOp and validatePaymasterUserOp to find the expensive branch.

title: AA41: too little verificationGas
summary: EntryPoint v0.6 could not complete UserOperation verification within the supplied verification gas budget.
likelyCauses: verificationGasLimit is too low for validateUserOp, paymaster validation, or signature checks.
The UserOperation changed after gas estimation, invalidating the previous estimate.
Account or paymaster validation takes a more expensive branch for the current state.
nextSteps: Estimate gas with the same EntryPoint, bundler, account state, signature, and paymaster data used for submission.
Raise verificationGasLimit if simulation shows verification gas exhaustion.
Trace the validation path if the required gas is unexpectedly high.

title: AA50: postOp reverted
summary: The paymaster's postOp hook reverted after execution, so the EntryPoint could not finish the sponsored operation accounting path.
likelyCauses: The paymaster postOp logic rejected the final gas cost, mode, token payment, or context.
The paymaster changed state between validation and postOp in a way that broke settlement.
A custom paymaster bug or external call inside postOp reverted.
nextSteps: Trace the paymaster postOp call and decode any inner revert emitted by the paymaster.
Check token balances, allowances, oracle prices, and policy state used by postOp settlement.
Escalate to the paymaster operator if the sponsorship service produced the paymaster data.

title: AA51: prefund below actualGasCost
summary: The actual gas cost of the UserOperation exceeded the prefund available from the smart account or paymaster deposit.
likelyCauses: Gas prices or execution gas exceeded the prefund calculated during validation.
The sender or paymaster deposit was too low for the final operation cost.
Gas limits were underestimated or the operation took a more expensive execution path.
nextSteps: Re-estimate the UserOperation gas and fees immediately before submission.
Top up the sender or paymaster EntryPoint deposit, depending on who is paying.
Reduce execution complexity or adjust gas limits if the operation regularly exceeds prefund.

title: AA90: invalid beneficiary
summary: The bundler or caller supplied an invalid beneficiary for handleOps, so EntryPoint cannot pay the collected fees.
likelyCauses: The beneficiary address is zero or otherwise invalid.
The bundler configuration did not set a valid fee recipient.
A custom handleOps caller passed the wrong beneficiary parameter.
nextSteps: Set a non-zero beneficiary address that can receive the EntryPoint payout.
If you do not operate the bundler, report the invalid beneficiary to the bundler or RPC provider.
Check custom handleOps integration code for the beneficiary argument.

title: AA91: failed send to beneficiary
summary: EntryPoint failed while sending collected fees to the beneficiary address supplied to handleOps.
likelyCauses: The beneficiary is a contract that rejects ETH or reverts in its receive path.
The beneficiary address is misconfigured by the bundler or custom handleOps caller.
The fee payout could not be completed after the operation accounting finished.
nextSteps: Use an externally owned account or a contract beneficiary that accepts ETH transfers.
If this came from a hosted bundler, report the beneficiary payout failure to the bundler operator.
Audit custom beneficiary contracts for receive/fallback reverts.

title: AA92: internal call only
summary: An EntryPoint helper intended only for internal execution, such as innerHandleOp, was called directly from outside the EntryPoint.
likelyCauses: A client or test harness called an internal EntryPoint function instead of handleOps or simulateValidation.
A low-level integration forwarded calldata to the wrong EntryPoint function selector.
The bundler or caller bypassed the public EntryPoint flow.
nextSteps: Call the public EntryPoint method intended for the workflow, such as handleOps or simulateValidation.
Check ABI/function selector routing in custom bundler or testing code.
Do not submit transactions directly to internal EntryPoint helper functions.

title: AA93: invalid paymasterAndData
summary: The paymaster data is missing, too short, or malformed for the EntryPoint version that is validating the UserOperation.
likelyCauses: EntryPoint v0.6 paymasterAndData is non-empty but shorter than the paymaster address payload.
EntryPoint v0.7/v0.8 paymaster fields were packed incorrectly or are missing required data.
The client mixed paymaster field formats across EntryPoint versions.
nextSteps: For v0.6, ensure paymasterAndData is empty or starts with a 20-byte paymaster address plus required data.
For v0.7/v0.8, verify paymaster, paymasterVerificationGasLimit, paymasterPostOpGasLimit, and paymasterData packing.
Regenerate sponsorship data from the paymaster service for the exact EntryPoint version.

title: AA94: gas values overflow
summary: One or more gas-related UserOperation fields exceed the numeric range that the EntryPoint can safely pack and validate.
likelyCauses: verificationGasLimit, callGasLimit, preVerificationGas, fee fields, or paymaster gas limits were set to unrealistic values.
A gas override or faulty estimator produced values larger than the EntryPoint's internal bounds.
The client mixed units or encoded gas fields incorrectly.
nextSteps: Remove manual gas overrides and re-run UserOperation gas estimation.
Check that all gas limit and fee fields fit within the EntryPoint version's documented integer bounds.
Use smaller gas values instead of trying to bypass estimation with very large numbers.

title: AA95: out of gas
summary: The EntryPoint handleOps execution ran out of gas for the operation or one of its sub-calls.
likelyCauses: The bundler or custom handleOps caller supplied too little transaction gas.
callGasLimit or another gas field is too low for the account execution path.
The target call consumed more gas than the simulation predicted.
nextSteps: Re-estimate the UserOperation gas with current calldata, account state, and chain fee conditions.
Increase the relevant gas limit only after identifying whether validation, execution, or postOp exhausted gas.
Optimize or split the target call if execution is genuinely too expensive.

title: AA96: invalid aggregator
summary: The signature aggregator address is invalid or reserved, so the EntryPoint cannot use it to validate aggregated signatures.
likelyCauses: The UserOperation references an aggregator address that does not implement the expected aggregator interface.
The aggregator field is set to a reserved marker address rather than a real aggregator.
The client selected an aggregator that is incompatible with this account or EntryPoint version.
nextSteps: Use an aggregator address that implements the ERC-4337 aggregator interface expected by the account.
Check that the account's signature mode actually requires an aggregator.
Remove aggregator data or regenerate the signature flow if the account validates signatures directly.
